title: House Robber
statement_short: Given an integer array nums representing the amount of money at each house, return the maximum amount of money you can collect without selecting two adjacent elements.
hint: Optimal subproblem state choice at index i is max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i]), demanding linear dynamic programming.
keywords: amount of money at each house
why_not: Right: 1D DP maintains max sum choices (selecting current element vs skipping current element) in O(n) time and O(1) space. Not Greedy: Picking the highest value element locally fails to maximize sum across non-adjacent combinations. Not Backtracking: Trying all select/skip combinations takes exponential O(2^n) time. Not Two Pointers: Scanning pointers cannot balance non-adjacent subproblem state transitions.
